question.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola Given a Graph
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13954664/assets/a16f3f2ba78b5aef180c4331d1dd99f37340d2c6d842c1596e35445f1dbf34c5.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(-4,0)$ and passes through the point $(8,6).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-4,0),$ we substitute $h=-4$ and $k=0$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(8,6),$ so we can substitute $x=8$ and $y=6$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ {6}^{2} & =4p(8+4) \\ 36 & =48p \\ p & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{3}{4})(x+4) \\ {y}^{2} & =3(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{3}{4}$ is positive.
